# Executive Summary

<!--
This section provides a condensed view of the entire proposal, one page long.
It should be a comprehensive high-level overview that captures the essence of the proposal, including its goals, methods, expected outcomes, deliverables, and budget.
-->
This proposal outlines a project to develop open-source R package to convert and construct Likert items from vectors or data frames, particularly from non-standard data structures. The proposal aims to bridge the gap where fragmented, manual workarounds that disrupt reproducible data workflows and introduce risks of manipulation errors are utilized for analyzing Likert-type data. The project will be executed over a nine-month timeline with a total proposed budget of USD 8,500. The timeline is divided into an initial two-month inception phase to design the architecture, a four-month coding and testing phase to release the core engine, a two-month preliminary release phase for initial CRAN submission and documentation setup, and a final month for project closure. The budget directly funds development labor at a rate of USD 50 per hour, documentation hosting, and a sensitization workshop for faculty and students at the Federal University of Technology, Minna. Upon completion, the package and its continuous updates will be maintained publicly in GitHub and CRAN repositories to optimize workflow efficiency for social and behavioral science researchers.
